stem: Which server does nslookup ask by default?

options.text: The default gateway, since routers forward every request
options.why: The gateway forwards packets; it is not necessarily a DNS server.

options.text: The first host that answers a ping on the local network
options.why: nslookup does not search for servers by pinging.

options.text: The DNS server configured on the PC, shown by ipconfig /all
The DHCP server, always, whatever the PC is configured to use
options.why: Only if that is what the PC was configured to use.

explain: nslookup uses the configured resolver unless you name another, as in nslookup fs-01 192.168.10.5.

stem: On Windows, which ping option sets the number of echo requests?

options.why: -l sets the payload size in bytes.
-w is the timeout per reply in milliseconds.

explain: ping -n 4 dc-01 sends four requests. Windows sends four by default; Linux ping runs until stopped.
